method: Cross-item test: for each unique entry_conditions[].object string across the 14 v3-shadow-specs fixtures (516 total rows, 456 unique object strings), check coverage against the pooled normalized-object-text corpus (the only prose field the v3 DecisionAtom spec.json schema carries — no entry_sequence/confluences prose exists in this pipeline; see project_spec_compiler_field_leak_audit_2026_07_03). Two logics compared: (A) pre-F-2 ORIGINAL substring `u.includes(normName) || nameWords.every(w=>u.includes(w))` at commit 15abe2d, (B) F-2 REMEDIATED exact-token+singularize logic in the current working tree (uncommitted, on top of HEAD 0db52b4). A flip = coveredA !== coveredB for at least one cross-item unit.

collision_correction.description: A=covered via mid-word/prefix substring collision with an UNRELATED word; B=missing. GOOD — the fix working as intended.

Not a flip (A also covered these via its whole-phrase u.includes(normName) or substring clause) — shown as corroborating evidence the singularizer is pulling real weight, capped at 15 examples.
